recommendation: Case-only or population-based design stated; if case-only, the conditioning on stroke and the possibility of collider stratification bias acknowledged
Effect of each genome-wide significant variant on stroke incidence reported from an independent incidence GWAS, or its unavailability stated as a limitation
Whether baseline severity was a covariate stated and its inclusion justified; its status as a mediator or collider acknowledged
At least one collider-bias correction (Slope-Hunter, Dudbridge or IPW) applied to the top hits with its assumptions and their plausibility, or the omission explained
Social determinants (socioeconomic position, access to care and rehabilitation, place of residence): whether measured, and whether treated as confounder, mediator or collider, with the reason
Exact phenotype definition: scale, time point of assessment and the Roundtable recovery phase it falls in, and ascertainment method (prospective, record review, ICD code)
Dichotomization and its cut-point stated; if ordinal analysis was used, whether the proportional-odds assumption was tested and held
For continuous phenotypes, the correlation between baseline severity and the follow-up measure, and whether baseline was a covariate
For a change score, σ₀, σ₁ and ρ of the two measurements, the identity value of the baseline-change correlation and its equal-variance null −√((1 − ρ)/2)

For a change score analyzed with, or adjusted for, its baseline: the reliability of the baseline instrument and the implied residual leakage ρ_T b₀(1 − λ) for the top loci, or the association repeated on a non-overlapping interval
Whether the GWAS phenotype is a change score, a follow-up score or a baseline-adjusted follow-up score, and the sign convention of the change
Correlation between the primary phenotype and any secondary phenotype used in the same study
For cohorts treated with drugs with known pharmacogenetic interactions (e.g., clopidogrel and CYP2C19), genotype-stratified analyses, or the reason they were not performed
Sample size per analysis (cases and controls, or effective sample size), separately by ancestry
Ancestry composition; whether the analysis was restricted to one ancestry, or the meta-analytic method used
Time window of outcome assessment, and whether it was fixed or variable across participants
Availability of severity data (NIHSS or equivalent) and whether they were used
For a proxy phenotype, its correlation with the construct of interest, or a statement that it is unknown
Genome-wide significance threshold and any adjustment beyond 5 × 10⁻⁸
Replication status of each genome-wide significant locus, with the replication sample size and ancestry; unreplicated loci stated as such
Effect size with confidence interval, or variance explained, for each reported locus - not only the p-value
For MR, TWAS and colocalization: the assumptions, the sensitivity analyses performed, and the conditions under which the results would not be interpretable
For a polygenic score: the ancestry of the discovery GWAS and of the target sample, and whether the score was validated in the target ancestry
For a multi-omic claim: the number and percentage of genes or proteins measured in both layers, and the compartment (tissue), construct, sampling time and Roundtable phase of each (Section 7)
